## Context
Jira DC summary updates can retry in both pycontribs/Jira and `_with_connection_retry`. The selected route needs a dedicated no-SDK-retry client and per-call wrapper policy without changing legacy callers.

## Outcome
Implement the DC summary executor with a guarded `max_retries=0` client and fixed GET -> PUT -> GET invocation. Ambiguous PUT recovery uses a separate single-attempt GET under the shared budget.

## Plan
1. Construct a dedicated executor client through the pinned public `jira.JIRA(..., max_retries=0)` argument; fail fast unless `_session.max_retries == 0`. Preserve legacy client construction.
2. Add an injected one-attempt/no-sleep policy to `_with_connection_retry` for selected executor calls; preserve legacy wrapper defaults.
3. Make one write invocation issue exactly GET/PUT/GET. A fault on the initial (pre-mutation) GET ends the invocation with `request_count=1`, classified as retryable (a transient transport fault mutated nothing, so replay is safe) or permanent (a definitive HTTP error). A fault on the PUT is ambiguous (the write may have landed) and ends the invocation `commit_unknown` with `request_count=2`, no read-back. On a successful PUT the read-back GET is authoritative and IS INSPECTED by comparing its observed summary against the intended new summary: the outcome is `applied` (`request_count=3`) ONLY when the observed summary EQUALS the intended new summary; if the read-back GET cannot be fetched, or its observed summary does NOT equal the intended value, the outcome is `commit_unknown` (`request_count=3`) — the write was accepted, so this layer neither claims success nor auto-replays.
4. After an ambiguous PUT, consume another physical invocation for one GET observation, mapped through the shared `decide_replay` table by the SAME comparison rule: the observation is `desired` when the observed summary EQUALS the intended new summary (→ `recovered`, no further write); `conclusive old state` when the observed summary is present but does NOT equal the intended value (→ replay within remaining budget, else exhausted); and `failed`/`inconclusive` when the GET itself raises (→ non-replaying `commit_unknown`).
5. Return classification/delay metadata to the shared owner; do not sleep or replay in SDK/adapter layers.
6. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every DC terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. Include only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; cap the whole serialized log at 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Testing
Use fake sessions with raw request counters and poison sleepers/retry adapters. Include the proven Jira 3.10.5 constructor/session guard plus completion-log field, cardinality, redaction, and size assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The dedicated executor client passes `max_retries=0` and rejects a nonzero session value.
- [x] Legacy DC client SDK retry remains unchanged.
- [x] Each selected write invocation is exactly GET/PUT/GET without hidden repeats.
- [x] Selected wrapper calls perform one attempt and no sleep, while legacy wrapper behavior remains unchanged.
- [x] Desired observation recovers without another write.
- [x] Conclusive old state permits only remaining-budget replay.
- [x] Failed or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`.
- [x] Every DC terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log with only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Out of scope
Core dispatch/handler integration and other DC operation families.
